corrected_value.authors: Wulff, Stephanie, Nick C. Ellis, Ute Römer, Kathleen Bardovi-Harlig and Chelsea J. Leblanc.
corrected_value.title: The acquisition of tense-aspect: Converging evidence from corpora and telicity ratings.

decisions.quote:
Prior research has found that the
      frequency and distinctiveness of verb forms in corpora of L1 English production predict L2
      English learners’ tense-aspect production (Wulff et al. 2009). The present study aims to replicate
      these findings and test the predictions of hypotheses of L2 tense-aspect acquisition in another
      group of learners: English-dominant, instructed Spanish learners.
decisions.location: Abstract, p. 156, lines 10-14 (and References, p. 184, lines 1244-1246)
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly replicates Wulff et al. (2009), cited in the reference list as 'Wulff, Stephanie, Nick C. Ellis, Ute Römer, Kathleen Bardovi-Harlig and Chelsea J. Leblanc. 2009. The acquisition of tense-aspect: Converging evidence from corpora and telicity ratings. The Modern Language Journal 93/3: 354–369.' (no DOI printed in text). Although the shipped row's outcome quote extracts the abstract sentence referring to Wulff et al. (2009), the shipped metadata misidentified that 2009 work as Gries & Wulff (2009) ('Psycholinguistic and corpus-linguistic evidence for L2 constructions', 10.1075/arcl.7.07gri), which is not cited in the paper. The blind coding accurately identified the replicated target.

decisions.quote:
In our data,
learners mirror the token and contingent frequency of verbs in the L1 corpus, providing
evidence that learning based on the properties of frequency and distinctiveness in L1
Spanish production occurs for the L2 Spanish acquisition of the preterit and the
imperfect. This finding proves that Wulff et al.’s (2009) conclusion for L2 English oral
production generalizes to L2 Spanish writing.
decisions.reason: With the dependent target identity resolved to Wulff et al. (2009), both the shipped row and the blind coding agree on 'successful'. The authors explicitly conclude in the Abstract and Section 6 that L1 Spanish verb token frequency and contingent frequency (distinctiveness) strongly predict L2 Spanish learners' emergent use of the preterit and imperfect, proving that Wulff et al.'s (2009) conclusion generalizes to L2 Spanish writing.

decisions.quote:
Prior research has found that the
      frequency and distinctiveness of verb forms in corpora of L1 English production predict L2
      English learners’ tense-aspect production (Wulff et al. 2009). The present study aims to replicate
      these findings and test the predictions of hypotheses of L2 tense-aspect acquisition in another
      group of learners: English-dominant, instructed Spanish learners. Analyses were performed on
      longitudinal data from the Corpus of Written Spanish of L2 and Heritage Speakers (COWS-L2H;
      Yamada et al. 2020) and cross-sectional data from the Corpus Escrito del Español L2 (CEDEL2;
      Lozano 2021).
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree that the record is a replication. The study tests whether the published finding of Wulff et al. (2009) holds in independent samples of L2 Spanish learners using new corpus data (COWS-L2H and CEDEL2).
